findings.reason: as written a node can land the fix in `dispatch_launch.py`, leave `gc.py` printing, pass every case and the control, and close §24 with the pane symptom the section exists to remove still reachable.
findings.text: §24's deliverable requires both `remove_worker_scratch` and `garbage_collect_scratch` to write nothing to stdout, but its three cases and its negative control cover only `remove_worker_scratch`: the control restores the print there alone, and the two `crew gc --scratch` cases assert only that a path is present "in the emitted JSON", which still holds while `reckon/crew/gc.py:1074` and `:1079` keep printing — and `gc.py:1074` emits the very string the section's Why quotes from the lead's pane (`removing worker scratch directory … (0 bytes)`), so the half that may have been the observed cause is the half no case fails on

findings.reason: the dispatch manifest contract requires `negative_control_log` as a bare path regardless of what the section says, so the evidence is produced without the plan naming it; the omission breaks the plan's own convention rather than the record.
findings.text: neither §24 nor §25 states where the negative-control log is written, where §§2–6, §15–§19, §21–§23 each end their done-when with "It is logged under the run directory"; §24 and §25 stop at "turns the first case red"

findings.reason: the deliverable is the stream-level row, the code verifiably appends one for an unchanged live run (`reckon/crew/runs.py:2110-2124`), so removing it is correct and harmless whatever the pane also does; only the Why's justification is unverified.
findings.text: §25 states "Those baselines are drawn" as the reason the section exists, but `RowPolicy` already drops a row that restates the state the pane shows (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1583-1590`), and §21 states that an in-place reload restores the pane's run states through the carried checkpoint and `follow_checkpoint.seed_states`, so a reload baseline for an unchanged run whose raw state is stable is suppressed at the pane; the observed `new → delivered` row therefore implies a pane with no memory of that run, which the Why does not say

response_events.reason: the lead observed the delivered run redrawn on a pane, so some pane held no memory of it (an observing session's pane or an attach whose checkpoint was lost); the stream-level row is what every such pane draws, and the finding itself grants that removing it at source is correct whatever the row policy does
